properties.usage: Empirical Bayes: events = births, population at risk = womenYears. Rate = births / womenYears x 1,000 = general fertility rate per year.
caveats: PEP births come from NCHS birth records; the most recent year is partly estimated.
Women 15-44 is a model-based estimate; in college towns students inflate it and lower the rate.
Contiguous US + DC; Connecticut as its 9 planning regions (Vintage 2023).
properties.sources: US Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program Vintage 2023 (co-est2023-alldata, cc-est2023-agesex-all), public domain
storyNotes: 10,842,553 births in 2021-2023; pooled general fertility rate 55.5 per 1,000 women aged 15-44 per year.
Median county population 26,132; median population of the top 5 % raw rates 6,374, of the bottom 5 % 50,052 (the low end is pulled by college towns, whose students inflate the denominator).
Counties under 5,000 residents (n=309): raw rates 43-103 (5th-95th pct) vs 42-68 over 100,000.
Highest raw rates: Petroleum, MT 163 (29 births); Dallam, TX 141 (543 births); Jackson, SD 138 (212 births); Hamlin, SD 126 (411 births); Geary, KS 122 (2922 births).
Lowest raw rates: Harding, NM 0 (0 births); Loving, TX 0 (0 births); Williamsburg, VA 12 (168 births); Manassas Park, VA 18 (193 births); Watauga, NC 22 (931 births).
2 counties recorded no births in three years; 36 fewer than 30.
